tokyo_oyasai_kozara_ryori_no_w.price_note: ⚠ TWO WARNINGS BEFORE THE PRICES. First, this menu carries an update date of 2017/09/28 — it is nearly nine years old, so treat every price as historical rather than current; the dishes are the shop's own text but the numbers will have moved. Second, THE SHOP'S OWN DOMAIN IS DEAD: vegan-kiboko.com no longer serves a site, returning a hosting error page reading ドメイン・ウェブの設定ができていません with the account described as non-existent, expired or deleted, and its TLS certificate belongs to the hosting provider (*.hpms1.jp) rather than the restaurant. Worth feeding to the dead-domain checker. The shop itself is trading — Tabelog carries the listing as 公式, closed Mondays, Tuesdays and Sundays. ⚠ HOW THE TWO DIETS SPLIT HERE: everything on this menu is vegan and a great deal of it is wheat. This is a vegetable wine bar built on gyoza wrappers, pasta and — most sharply — 車麩, which is pure wheat gluten and entirely plant-based. A vegan will eat very well; a coeliac vegan needs to read item by item, and the steamed vegetables are the safest thing on the page.

It is perfectly vegan and completely out for a coeliac, and its name gives no warning in either language. The かば焼 preparation adds a second route: 甘辛く煮た means simmered in a soy-and-sugar glaze. Vegan on the shop's own blanket statement: 「動物性食材、卵、乳製品を使用せず」 and 「全てベジタリアン、ヴィーガン、ハラール、対応料理です」 — no animal ingredients, no egg, no dairy, across the whole board.

tokyo_aburasoba_sohonten_shinj.price_note: Read from the chain's own site (東京油組総本店). CHAIN-WIDE MENU, NOT BRANCH-SPECIFIC: this record is the Shinjuku East Exit Alta-ura branch, and the board below is the one the chain publishes across its shops, so a branch may vary. No allergen statement anywhere on the site. ⚠ THIS IS A WHEAT SHOP AND THERE IS NO WAY AROUND IT — worth saying plainly rather than burying in per-item notes. 油そば is brothless wheat ramen tossed in a soy-based tare; the noodle and the sauce are both out, and the shop sells nothing a coeliac can build a meal from. It is recorded in full anyway so the answer is visible rather than absent. One genuinely useful quirk: 並盛り 160g, 大盛り 240g and W盛り 320g ALL COST THE SAME, so portion size is free. Two free toppings, すりニンニク and 柚子こしょう, are the only items on the page with no wheat route.

items.en: Aburasoba — brothless noodles in the house tare; regular 160g, large 240g and double 320g all the same price
items.note: Aburasoba noodles are WHEAT — the chain's own strapline is 麺が美味しい油そばといえば, the noodle is the point of the shop, and 油そば has never meant buckwheat. The 特製タレ is a soy-and-vinegar sauce, so the dressing is wheat as well as the noodle. Standard service includes chashu, which is soy-braised pork.

items.en: Spicy miso aburasoba — same three portion sizes, same price across them
items.note: Aburasoba noodles are WHEAT — the chain's own strapline is 麺が美味しい油そばといえば, the noodle is the point of the shop, and 油そば has never meant buckwheat. Miso adds a second route worth knowing: Japanese miso is frequently 麦味噌, which is BARLEY — and barley is not on Japan's statutory allergen list, so no label will flag it.
